videos.script:
This lesson is about data that does not fit in one piece. {{bytes}} It starts with bytes. A string is text, a Buffer is bytes, and the word "olá" is three of one and four of the other. Half the bugs with files and sockets live in that difference.

{{files}} Then files. Three ways to read one, the paths that keep a client inside a folder, and the error codes a program decides on. {{crash}} Then the write that a crash can tear in half. You will kill a program in the middle of saving, and lose the old data and the new at once. And then the fix, a rename, which the links service uses from today to keep its links on disk.

{{streams}} Then streams. A log of a hundred and thirty megabytes, counted twice. Once read whole, once a piece at a time, with the memory each one needed. {{pressure}} Then the boolean that write returns, and what happens to a server that ignores it.

{{http}} And last, a request and a response are streams too. A download that never holds the file, and an upload stopped at its limit.
